content:
1	Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs) are a leading cause of hospital admissions and healthcare costs.
     2	Traditional methods of ADR reporting often rely on post-marketing surveillance, and manual reporting
     3	of ADRs to the local or national pharmacovigilance agencies for causality assessment and final
     4	reporting to the WHO. High-income countries have their own national (i.e., USFDA) and regional
     5	(i.e., European Medicines Agency / EMA) pharmacovigilance agencies. However, this process is slow
     6	and inefficient. This article proposes a novel framework for integrating ADR detection into clinical
     7	workflows using Electronic Medical Record (EMR) systems, crowdsourced reporting from patients and
     8	healthcare professionals, and graph theory for generating automated ADR signals and reports to the
     9	local or national pharmacovigilance agencies. The system leverages automated data collection from
    10	EMRs (drug prescriptions, clinical notes) by EMR data scraping, integrating ADR dictionaries and
    11	drug databases to automate the generation of ranked ADR signals. By applying graph theory, the
    12	system filters and upranks connections between drugs and ADRs, considering the temporal relationship
    13	between drug administration and ADR occurrence. This automated approach offers a significant
    14	improvement in ADR reporting, enabling faster detection and more accurate predictions.
    15	Methodologies, framework visualizations and python code snippets are included to aid implementation.

Based solely on `doc.txt`, the relationship is as follows:

The document describes a novel framework for integrating Adverse Drug Reaction (ADR) detection into clinical workflows. This framework uses:
- Electronic Medical Record (EMR) systems, with automated data collection (drug prescriptions, clinical notes) via EMR data scraping
- Crowdsourced reporting from patients and healthcare professionals
- Graph theory to generate automated ADR signals and reports, filtering and upranking connections between drugs and ADRs while considering the temporal relationship between drug administration and ADR occurrence
- ADR dictionaries and drug databases to automate the generation of ranked ADR signals

The python code snippets relate to this framework as an implementation aid. The final line of the document states: "Methodologies, framework visualizations and python code snippets are included to aid implementation." In other words, the code snippets are provided alongside the methodologies and framework visualizations specifically to help implement the proposed ADR-detection framework.

Note that the document does not describe the contents of the code snippets in any further detail — it only states that they are included to aid implementation of the framework.
